You're a good girl. A fine child. Children like you are this nation's greatest treasure. Grow up healthy and strong.
SIGMUND TO ANYA FORGER[1]

Sigmund Authen (ジークムント・オーセン, Jīkumunto Ōsen?) is an elderly man who is the husband of Barbara Authen and the Forger family's new neighbor. Yor and Anya help him get home after he gets lost in the city. He was a university lecturer during his prime, specializing in neurology but dabbled in cultural anthropology.


ADVERTISEMENT
Appearance

Sigmund is a short, elderly man with heavy wrinkles, being about a head taller than Anya. His hair is receding and messy, and he has a big, bushy beard and thick, drooping eyebrows alongside round-framed glasses with a high bridge.

Sigmund typically wears a cardigan over a V-neck sweater with a collared shirt underneath.
Personality

Sigmund and Anya are delighted with their lesson
Sigmund and Anya's common joy in their lesson
Despite his aging memory and being past his prime, Sigmund is still quite an intelligent man and can effectively teach others. Sigmund has a passion for learning, believing that it is one of the fundamental joys of being human, and he wishes to learn as much as he can. He shares this passion with those he teaches, as he shows them the importance of finding the joys of learning by making their lessons palatable to them in a way they can understand the material and also make it fun for them. Also, Sigmund does not skimp on praise when he sees the student's progress in their studies. During the lessons with Anya, he approves her progress with words or by tousling her hair affectionately, believing that she is doing a hard job.

It also seems Sigmund hopes for a peaceful future for Ostania after the wars. He has a soft side for children and believes that they are his nation's greatest treasure.
ADVERTISEMENT

History

Sigmund is a highly regarded scholar and mainly worked in neurology. He also dabbled in other subjects like cultural anthropology and claims to have once toured the world to study local folk remedies as a fieldwork project. In his prime, Sigmund was a university professor and taught neurology and other subjects in Berlint, where he lived for a long time. At some point in his younger years, he married his wife, Barbara, and the two had a son.

Sigmund appears to have lived through both wars between the East and West. While walking through the district where his university is, he vividly remembers how the district was hit hard by the war and how the people reacted during those dark times. During the second war, Sigmund and Barbara went to Covenia, where Sigmund helped rehabilitate wounded soldiers. The couple eventually moved to the region for work, but when it came time to retire, they decided to return to Berlint to be closer to their son and his family.
Synopsis

Term Finals Arc

Sigmund's Thoughts
Sigmund gets lost at the park
Sigmund and Barbara move to 128 Park Avenue in the unit next to the Forger family. While moving in, Sigmund leaves to do some shopping at the market. On the way there, he starts craving sweets and buys some at the nearby candy shop. However, because of his poor memory, Sigmund forgets his task and wanders to a park. Realizing he is lost, he resigns himself to feeding his sweets to the pigeons. Sigmund does not stay for long, as he gets chased away by two boys who believe he is a suspicious spy. Sigmund eventually returns to the park and enters the playground, which he believes is his home. After getting stuck on the log bridge, Sigmund quickly comes to his senses and panics. After Yor helps him down, Sigmund explains to her and Anya that he cannot return home as he is unable to remember anything.

Yor tries to help him jog his memory, but Sigmund cannot think of any helpful information when Anya reads his mind. Yor asks if Sigmund has anything on him that could help, prompting the old man to dig through his pocket and find a shopping list. Sigmund loudly shouts "Eureka!" as he remembers his shopping plan, so the Forgers decide to take him to the nearest marketplace. Before they go, Sigmund begins mumbling about how to repay the family and contemplates adding them to his will. Reading his mind, Anya tells Yor what Sigmund mentioned, but Yor politely declines.

Yor, Anya, Bond, and Sigmund run from a mafia
Yor, Anya, Bond, and Sigmund run from a mafia after accidentally walking in on them
At the marketplace, Sigmund buys his groceries. As the group walks around the place together, Sigmund looks around and comments on how much the area has changed over the years. He then reveals that he used to teach at the university nearby and mumbles how badly it was affected during the war. As the group walks around the market, Anya continues reading Sigmund's thoughts to help guide Yor to places they should check out, but they end up back at the park. They try again but find themselves at a mafia branch office, where the members mistake them for enemies and begin shooting at them, but Yor quickly carries everyone away. After getting away, Sigmund goes to a flower shop after smelling Barbara's favorite flowers, but Yor stops him. Following his and Anya's directions one more time, the group goes to the top of a tower, with Sigmund insisting that his apartment is here.

Sigmund buys Anya waffles
Sigmund buys Anya waffles
They eventually sit down to rest, and Sigmund becomes gloomy for causing the family so much trouble. However, Anya tells him she had fun in this "adventure." Sigmund thanks Anya for not mocking his failings and buys her a waffle, mentioning that he sees her like a granddaughter. After Anya gets her waffle, Sigmund puts his wallet back in his pocket, and Yor notices a piece of paper fall from it. After seeing that it is a coupon, Anya proudly reveals that it is a winning ticket from the raffle at the candy shop she goes to. Sigmund remembers that he went to the candy shops, giving the group a clue to the location of his home. Bond suddenly goes off on his own, and Yor, deducing that he found the man's scent trail, follows after him with the others.

The group arrives at their apartment, which Sigmund says is his home, but a dumbfounded Yor believes he is mistaken. To everyone's surprise, a door opens to reveal Barbara with Loid, who has been helping her move in. Sigmund happily reunites with Barbara, who is confused about where he has been. After Loid explains the situation, Sigmund and Yor are surprised to be neighbors. The Authens introduce themselves to the Forgers, who welcome them to the neighborhood. To apologize to Barbara, Sigmund gifts her flowers that he managed to get during his journey. Barbara accepts his apology, and the two begin to flirt affectionately as the Forgers watch.[2]

Chapter 91
The Authens meet the Forgers in the morning
One morning, the Authens reunite with Yor and Anya, who are off to have their respective days. Upon seeing her school uniform, the pair learn that Anya is a student at Eden Academy. Sigmund then comments that Yor is going to work early, to which Yor responds that she will be helping hold an event at the city square. Barbara recognizes the event as the charity bazaar for disabled veterans, and Yor invites them to come. Sigmund expresses support but begins muttering about bringing a lunch, which Anya relays to Yor.[3]

As Anya and Loid prepare for the former's term finals, they get a surprise visit from the Authens, who invite the Forgers over to have cookies and get to know them better. Noticing that Anya is in the middle of studying, Sigmunds suggests taking a break, and Lois accepts their invitation. At the Authens' home, the neighbors chat over cookies. Loid brings up Sigmund's large collection of books, prompting them to talk about his time as a university professor. When Loid mentions Classical Language, Anya exclaims that her goal is to get the top grade in that subject. Sigmund offers to help Anya study, and Loid allows them.

Sigmund shows Anya Spy Wars volume
Sigmund teaches Anya using a volume of Spy Wars
Sigmund starts by asking Anya her favorite book. Anya says Spy Wars, so Sigmund reveals the first volume of the comic to use as their textbook. At Sigmund's instruction, he and Anya repeat a Bondman quote in the classical language. When Anya makes a mistake, he teaches her how to properly use the language. Loid interjects when he thinks the lesson might be getting too complicated, but Sigmund encourages Anya to find joy in studying. As Sigmund resumes their lesson, Barbara remarks how happy he looks while teaching her.

Sigmund hugs Anya
Sigmund hugs Anya
After a fun and successful lesson with Sigmund, Anya and her parents make their leave, with Sigmund offering to teach her again. Anya accepts the offer, saying she will come every day so she can earn a Stella Star. Sigmund asks what Anya will do after she aces her exams and becomes an Imperial Scholar and what her goal is. After turning to her parents, she replies that she wants world peace. Sigmund is happy with Anya's answer and hugs her, saying that children like her are the nation's greatest treasure. For the next few days, Sigmund assists Anya with her studies to get the top grade in Classical Language. On the day of the exams, a rugged Anya tells the Authens that she will bring back Stellas, and the two cheer her on.[1]

Anya thinks she will get Sigmund's estate
Sigmund denies talking to Anya about his estate
When the exam results are announced, Anya is overjoyed to learn that she got a Stella Star after earning second place in Classical Language (and shocked to be getting a Tonitrus after failing her Math exam). At home, Anya is congratulated for her achievement by her parents and the Authens, with Sigmund saying that Anya has now learned the joy of being rewarded for hard work, which he says is more valuable than Stella. He adds that Anya will one day experience the frustration of not all hard work being rewarded, but says that learning it is also a treasure. Anya misunderstands his statement and asks if this treasure is him willing his estate, which Sigmund says he did not say at all.[4]

ADVERTISEMENT

Abilities and Skills

Teaching: Due to his background in neurology and his exploration of other fields, Sigmund's experience in both academic and fieldwork settings gave him impressing teaching skills, becoming an university professor. He later helps study Anya classical language, and thanks to his knowledge and interactive way of explaining the subject, Anya gets a high score and even is awarded with a Stella.
Weaknesses

Age: Due to his old age, Sigmund's memory is not very good. He is very forgetful, not being able to remember recent details such as the address of the home he recently moved into and tasks he planned to do for the day. However, Sigmund seems to remember his past a bit more, recalling his experiences in the wars quite vividly.
Relationships

Barbara Authen

The Forgers are looking at the Authens' reunion
The Forgers watch Sigmund and Barbara flirting together
Barbara is Sigmund's wife. Sigmund greatly cherishes her, thinking of and missing her when he gets lost in their new neighborhood, even bringing her flowers as an apology when they reunite. Due to his poor memory, Sigmund often looks to Barbara for clarification or correction on past events or people's names. When they were younger, Sigmund used to be away from home all the time due to his work, though this did not appear to strain their relationship. The two are quite flirtatious, not minding to show off how affectionate they are in public. Sigmund and Barbara have a son together and have moved to Berlint to be closer to him and his family.

Anya Forger

Sigmund, nicknamed "Grandpa Siggy" by Anya, is the little girl's elderly neighbor. The two first meet when Sigmund gets lost in the park shortly after moving into 128 Park Avenue. As the Forgers try to help Sigmund get back home, Anya acts as his interpreter for Yor when he begins mumbling, though she often tends to misunderstand what he says. During their search, Sigmund is grateful that Anya does not make fun of him for his failings and begins seeing her as a granddaughter, doting on her as such.

Sigmund tousles Anya's hair
Sigmund approves of Anya's progress in their lesson
Sigmund later becomes Anya's Classical Language tutor in preparation for her term finals. He teaches her the joy of studying, using her favorite series as their textbook, and does not forget to praise her for her progress. Sigmund later asks Anya what her ultimate goal is after her school achievements, and she answers "world peace," which greatly satisfies him. Anya earns a Stella Star from her Classical Language grades, Sigmund and Barbara sincerely congratulate the young girl.

However, despite his good-natured attitude towards Anya, Sigmund also tends to be judgmental when he thinks that she says unacceptable things. For example, when Anya believes that Sigmund will give her a lot of money, he quickly denies saying such things to her.

Aaron (アーロン, Āron?) is one of the supporting characters of the SPY x FAMILY series. He is the pet dog of Sylvia Sherwood.

In the past, like Bond Forger, he was a victim of the cruel experiments of Project Apple and was later used as one of the bomb dogs for the Berlint University terrorist group, led by Keith Kepler, in their plot to assassinate Minister Brantz.


ADVERTISEMENT
Appearance

Aaron is a large male German Shepherd. He has a domed forehead, a long square-cut muzzle with strong jaws, and a black nose. The eyes are medium-sized and yellow. The ears are large and stand erect, open at the front and parallel. Aaron's coat is tan and black, he has a typical black mask and black body marking in the form of a "saddle" on his back, characteristic of his breed.
Personality

Aaron is an easygoing dog. In the possession of Keith and his group, he was trained as an aggressive fighter as well as an effective tracker and bomb dog. He was brave enough to attack Loid Forger, who was shooting at him, and charged at him head-on. Despite that, he was genuinely scared by the angry Yor who defended Anya from him and Keith, and this was enough to escape from his then-owner.

The Forgers recognize Aaron
A noticeable difference between Aaron's current friendly side and his former aggressive behavior
After being captured by WISE and subsequently adopted by Sylvia, Aaron became more friendly and playful. His great emotionality was also shown when he was shocked and offended that Sylvia did not clean their apartment, that Bond did not recognize him, and that Sylvia chose his name in a rather careless way.

Aaron, like Bond, is a mentally enhanced intelligent dog but is not as forgetful as the latter.
ADVERTISEMENT

Abilities and Skills

Aaron's time as a research experiment left him with above-average intelligence for a dog. He is capable of understanding human speech.

Sense of Smell: He is an excellent tracker who easily tracked down Anya, Bond, and even the smell of a target from far distances.

Loid tries to shoot at the dog
Loid tries to shoot at Aaron
Basic Combat Training: Due to his past as a research subject for military purposes, Aaron might have already been trained in basic combat abilities.

Speed and Reactions: While chasing Loid, he was fast enough to catch up with him much quicker than Keith did in his car and later showed impressive agility when he dodged Loid's gunfire at medium range.
Relationships

Sylvia Sherwood

Sylvia and Aaron are going to meet with Loid
Aaron is happily going for a walk with Sylvia
Aaron and Sylvia are in a close, almost familial relationship. After she promised Anya to take care of other dogs after the foiled assassination attempt on the minister, she adopted Aaron and settled him in her apartment. The dog looks healthy and happy because Sylvia takes good care of him and sometimes even refuses to meet with colleagues at work to pay attention to him. However, sometimes Aaron has complaints about her, for example, when she brings their house to a mess or because of the fact that she did not choose his name too carefully. Also, they both appear to share a common passion for competition and rivalry when they were determined to defeat Loid and Bond together.

Loid Forger

Their relationship was initially hostile since Aaron perceived Loid as Minister Brantz, his target whose scent he was trained to track. Even after Loid revealed that he was not the minister, Aaron continued his attack and bit on Loid's arm. Loid initially tried to shoot Aaron but later chose to save him by removing the bomb from him and simply closing him in a dumpster. After some time, under the influence of Sylvia, Aaron stopped being aggressive and, during his reunion with Loid, showed him friendliness, letting go of the past.

Bond Forger

Anya plays with Aaron and Bond
Aaron plays with Bond and Anya
Since Aaron and Bond were both fellow subjects of Project Apple, the two have been together for a long time.[1] During their stay with the terrorists, Aaron did not show aggression toward Bond until he treacherously escaped from them to save Anya. He began to regard him as an enemy and was ready to pounce on him on Keith's orders. Later, together with Sylvia, Aaron met Bond again at the dog park and seemed glad to see him, but almost started another fight after being upset at Bond's forgetfulness. He was also determined to beat Bond in their competition in the park, however, when their rival confrontation ended, he again forgot all grievances and continued to play with his newfound friend.

Anya Forger

In their first meeting, Aaron and Anya did not show much interest in each other because the girl liked Bond more, and he did not show any aggression towards her. However, on Keith's orders, he was ready to kill her without hesitation had he not been stopped and scared off by the terrifying Yor. After being taken in by Sylvia and reuniting with Anya at the dog park, Aaron showed his playful side and happily played with her and Bond.

entries.name: Barbara Authen
entries.content:
Barbara Authen is an elderly woman who is Sigmund's wife and the Forger family's new neighbor. Loid helps her move in when the couple arrives at their unit.

The first part of Barbara's name in Japanese (バー, Bā?) is a pun of (ばば, Baba?), an informal word for Grandma. Her last name could be a pun on Authentic.
After their meeting, Anya starts calling her "Grandma Barbara," or "Granny Barb" (バーばば, Bā baba?).

How I hope that these children are able to remain forever unbounded by the statures and standpoints of their parents, and continue seeking out their own happiness of their own accord. It may not be my place to hope for such things, but I cannot help but wish it all the same.
JEEVES ABOUT DAMIAN DESMOND AND THE OTHER CHILDREN[1]

Jeeves (ジーブス, Jivuzu?) is a butler for the Desmond Family, typically serving as Damian's attendant.


ADVERTISEMENT
Appearance


1/2


Jeeves is a tall, handsome man with dark blue eyes and neatly styled black hair swept to the left side of his head. He is always seen dressed in a black tuxedo with a tie, consistently maintaining a formal appearance in the presence of the Desmond family.
Personality

Jeeves is a highly skilled and dependable butler, characterized by his commitment to the Desmond family. Despite his role as a servant, Jeeves exhibits remarkable initiative and resourcefulness, capable of adapting to any situation—whether preparing gourmet meals in the middle of a forest or using his quick reflexes to protect Damian from danger. His ability to stay calm under pressure, combined with his physical endurance and strength, makes him a formidable presence.

Damian tells Jeeves they can't go back yet
Jeeves worries for Damian
Jeeves also seems to have a close and communicative relationship with both Melinda and Damian, often discussing Damian's daily activities with Melinda and relying on her judgment for matters concerning the family, as seen when she personally selects cakes at her son's request, which Jeeves then delivers. While he maintains a professional distance, Jeeves's actions reveal a deep sense of loyalty and care for the Desmonds, particularly towards Damian, whom he constantly watches over and protects. Being aware of the estrangement between the Desmonds, Jeeves worries for Damian and knows he seeks a familial bond with them, so he often tries to cheer him up, even if it means lying to him about his parents.
ADVERTISEMENT

Abilities and Skills

Enhanced Physical Abilities: Jeeves appears to have basic combat skills and impressive reflexes, as demonstrated when he swiftly threw an acorn at a snake that was about to attack Damian, successfully immobilizing it. He also displays considerable endurance and strength, effortlessly carrying a heavy bag on his back for extended periods while constantly chasing after Damian to keep him safe.

Butlers cooking for the children
Jeeves showing his cooking skills
Cooking: As a butler, Jeeves possesses exceptional cooking skills and is prepared to whip up any meal on demand. Even in the middle of a forest, Jeeves and the other butlers effortlessly unpack their cooking tools from their bags and prepare a gourmet dish for the children.
Relationships

Damian Desmond

Damian agrees with Jeeves's thoughts on Donovan
Jeeves assures Damian that his parents care
Jeeves normally serves under the instructions of Damian, whom he has nicknamed as "Master Dammy."[2] Being aware of the estrangement between the Desmonds, he tries to guide and cheer Damian, doing his best to make him believe Donovan is looking out for him and assuring him that Melinda, despite her absence, still cares about him. Jeeves also wishes for Damian to be unburdened by his family's reputation and able to find his own happiness in life, so he takes joy in seeing his young master acting like any other normal child would and being himself around his friends. Since Jeeves likes to satisfy Damian's childish desires, he has been called out by other butlers for coddling the boy too much.

On occasions, Jeeves accompanies Damian to places where he needs protection. When accompanying Damian, Jeeves often acts as a voice of reason to the boy and will try to dissuade him from immature acts. Aware of Damian's aspiration to one day become a politician and statesman like his father, Jeeves tries to instruct him on how to act as one, though his advice can be quite blunt as he calls the people he will have to rule over "those below" and "the common folk."

Melinda Desmond

Although Jeeves and Melinda have not been shown interacting directly, it is evident that they communicate more frequently than he does with Donovan. Jeeves often discusses Damian's day with Melinda, including incidents like the day Anya punched Damian, much to the boy's annoyance. When Damian asks Jeeves for a favor, it seems Melinda is the one who often takes action, as in the case when Damian requested cakes for Anya, Jeeves mentioned that it was Melinda who personally selected the cakes, not him.

Demetrius Desmond

Almost nothing is known of their relationship, although it seems Jeeves has also served Demetrius, who, like Damian, has been nicknamed "Master Demmy" by him.[2] He is seen in the past accompanying him and Donovan during one of their study sessions.

Donovan Desmond

Jeeves serves as the Desmonds' servant, including Donovan. Jeeves often reports to Donovan about how his sons are doing at Eden Academy, even mentioning to him the incident Damian had on the first day of school.

OLKA TO YOR FORGER[1]

Olka Gretcher (オルカ・グレッチャー, Oruka Gurecchā?) is one of the last two remaining members of the Gretcher crime family alongside her only son Gram Gretcher.

Looking to leave her old life behind with her son, Olka becomes Yor Forger's client and is placed under the assassin's protection from hitmen while aboard the Princess Lorelei cruise ship to seek asylum in another country. She and her follower Zeb traveled as the "Grey Family," with Olka using the alias Shaty Grey (シャティ・グレイ, Shati Gurei?) and pretending to be Zeb's wife.


ADVERTISEMENT
Appearance


00:00

41:20

Olka is a young woman wearing glasses with short hair and messy bangs. However, her current appearance is a disguise to help her travel incognito. In an old photo of her, she is shown to originally have long black hair tied into a low ponytail.

Due to her need to hide and avoid the assassins, Olka constantly changed her clothes, not having any standard clothing. In her first appearance, her clothing consisted of an open white coat with a dress and black heels[2], and later wore a red dress in the evening. Before leaving the ship, she puts on a black wig tied with a bow on the back.[3]
Personality

Olka is shown to be a kind and generous woman who is willing to do anything to protect the ones she loves and to save anyone who is needed, as she gave Zeb some food to save him when they were younger. When Yor first met her, she seemed quite serious and direct (and is understood as she lost most of her family), but she still was kind toward her and respected her motives. As time passes by, Olka begins to trust more in Yor and her capabilities, but also starts feeling fright for everything going around the cruise and her situation, but tries her best to stay calm and relaxed to keep her child calm too.
ADVERTISEMENT

History

The Gretcher family used to manage Ostania's underworld in an honorable fashion. Olka grew up during the second war between Ostania and Westalis, and her family ran a black market that distributed food to people on the streets after it ended. During this time, Olka encountered Zeb and secretly gave him a loaf of bread to eat, earning his loyalty.

Olka Gretcher Original Appearance Anime
Olka (before changing her appearance) and Gram
In a recent incident, Olka's father and two brothers were killed in an internal dispute. Shortly after, Leonardo Hapoon took over the organization and put a bounty on Olka and Gram's heads. Going into hiding, the two sought temporary shelter in a safe house. Wanting to leave her life behind and live peacefully with Gram, Olka chose to escape and seek asylum in a foreign country, by being a passenger of the Princess Lorelei, where at the port of disembarkation, she will take another ship that will take her to the country. Olka and Gram are accompanied by Zeb, who pretends to be her husband, and the three disguise themselves as the "Grey Family." As a favor to her father, the Shopkeeper of the Garden assigns two of his assassins to bodyguard her on the ship.[4]
ADVERTISEMENT

Synopsis

Cruise Adventure Arc

Matthew and Yor meet Zeb and the Gretchers
The Gretchers and Zeb meet Matthew and Yor
Under the guise of being hosted for an enticement campaign, the Greys board Princess Lorelei. At their room, they meet with the group from Berlint City Hall, with Matthew McMahon (the other bodyguard for the Gretchers) introducing himself as the Director of Policy, two oblivious bureaucrats from their business development team, and Yor Forger to assist Olka. Zeb, now going by Furseal Grey, presents himself as a member of Arhaus Department Stores and Olka as his wife, Shaty. The two bureaucrats offer to give the Greys a tour of the ship, though Olka refuses while citing the need to take care of her baby.

Alone with Yor, Olka watches the assassin inspect the suite for possible entry and escape routes. The two begin to talk, with Yor accidentally calling her Olka, which the latter quickly corrects. Olka reveals Furseal's true identity and talks about her desire to live a quiet life with her son. Olka then requests that she and her son go outside briefly. Yor is initially hesitant, but Olka says their enemy does not know what she looks like and knows that Yor will protect her, and Yor accepts. As they prepare to leave, Yor nervously looks around outside the door. Olka questions her suspicious-looking actions and is surprised to learn that Yor has a family who are also aboard the ship.

Yor and the Gretchers are on the deck
Yor accompanies Olka and Gram as they go outside
Yor explains to Olka that her family's presence on the ship is a coincidence and that they are unaware of her real job. Olka sees Yor's nervousness and asks if they are only for her cover identity, which Yor answers with a tender look. Gram starts to cry, reminding Yor of their plan to go outside. Olka stops Yor to lend some clothes for a disguise. When they go outside for fresh air, Olka is wistful about leaving her old life behind. Her son starts to sneeze, so they decide to head back. Yor promises to give it her all and finish the job for Olka and her son. Her words move Olka, so she reveals Gram's name and offers to let Yor hold him on their way back.[2]

Later, the city hall group and the Grey family have dinner at a fancy restaurant. After dinner, Yor escorts Olka and Gram back to their room. Once inside, Olka notes there has not been any sign of trouble the entire day, but Yor warns her that they must keep their guard up as they have no idea of where the enemy is or their plan. She predicts that the enemy will try attacking at the last possible minute on the next day. Olka asks what everyone else will do if she manages to escape safely, and Yor explains their prepared cover story. Olka then asks if Yor will see her family after she completes her mission, as the ship will stop at a resort island on the third day. She suggests that Yor could use it to spend time with her family, though Yor is hesitant about it. As Olka decides to get changed for the night, the women hear a mysterious knock on the door.[5]

Yor saves the Gretchers from gun shots
Yor moves Olka and Gram out of the line of fire
Yor looks through the peephole and sees a waiter with room service. Yor is relieved and informs Olka, who says she did not order anything. Yor hears a gun click behind the door and quickly moves Olka and Gram to safety, much to her shock. Matthew and Yor kill the assassin and retrieve his corpse, after which Matthew informs the group that the itinerary got leaked and there are multiple enemies aboard the ship. He directs Yor to take Olka, Gram, and Zeb to a vacant room in the second-class suite while he covers up the mess. After receiving domino masks to disguise themselves, Yor, Olka, Zeb, and Gram leave for the second deck lounge.

At the lounge, which is hosting a masquerade ball, the group passes through the area. An assassin is dispatched to kill Olka, but Yor stops him, grabbing his hand. She acts as if she was invited to a dance and dances the man away from Olka. Yor returns to her, Gram, and Zeb and guides them through the shopping promenade to the second-class area.[6] There, Yor protects the group from a surprise attack by the assassin, Sickle-and-Chain Barnaby[7]. Yor defeats him before resuming their move to the new room.[8]

Young Olka Gretcher Anime
A young Olka in Zeb's memory
After arriving at their new room, Yor assures the group that it is secure and has everything they need to hole up safely until the rendezvous. Gram starts to cry in fear, and Olka tries to comfort him, though she herself is also terrified. Zeb notices them and begins exclaiming how scared he was of their attackers. Olka and Gram disapprove of Zeb's cowardice, while he is satisfied seeing them calm down.

Olka asks Zeb why he came with them instead of joining the gang's new boss. Zeb says he does not forget how much he owes to the previous boss. He recalls how he would have been dead if not for the black market the Gretcher family ran after the war and flashes back to a young Olka secretly giving him bread. Zeb remembers this fondly and says it is all the reason he needs to be with her. Zeb promises to protect Olka from harm but quickly becomes scared when he hears a knock on the door and hides behind Olka. Behind the door is Matthew, who instructs Olka and the others to rest while he and Yor stand on guard. Olka goes to bed with Gram, but she does not sleep.[9]

Episode 32-6
The group moves out to prepare for the rendezvous
On the second day, Olka and the others wait in the room until they get a call from Matthew. Yor answers the phone and informs the others that they got the all-ready signal from the ship at the rendezvous. While it will be in four hours, Yor tells Olka and Zeb to prepare and change into their disguises. After seeing that the coast is clear, Yor, Olka, Gram, and Zeb head out.[10]

As the fireworks show is about to commence, the group walks through the ship's halls to get to Storage Area 3, where Olka will depart from the boat and to the rendezvous ship, hoping to proceed under the cover of the fireworks. As the show starts, the group is startled by the sudden noise and Gram starts to cry, so Olka coos her baby telling him how beautiful the fireworks are. After calming down, they continue onward. From above, a sniper watches them and prepares to shoot Olka as another firework goes off. Yor quickly grabs Olka out of the way but gets grazed by the shot. After fending off another assassin, Yor asks Olka and the others if they are alright. Suddenly, a large number of assassins reveal themselves and surround the group.[11]

Zeb protects Olka and Gram
Zeb uses his body to shield Olka and Gram
As assassins surround them, the group is saved by Matthew's arrival, who obtains a sniper and begins killing their foes. He shoots open a nearby hatch, which Yor orders the others to hide inside. However, while Yor gets held back by interferences from other assassins, Olka, Gram, and Zeb are confronted by an assassin aiming his gun at them. Zeb quickly grabs Olka and shields her from the bullets fired. As they tumble inside the hatch, Zeb shuts the cover. Olka worriedly asks Zeb if he is okay, but he reveals that he wore a bulletproof vest and complains about the pain, prompting Olka to scold him for being so reckless.[12]

The Gretchers say goodbye to Yor
Olka thanks Yor for ensuring her son's future
After Yor and Matthew exterminate all the enemy assassins, Olka and Zeb are retrieved from the hatch and head to the storage area, where Yor and Matthew prepare the inflatable boat for them. While Matthew gives Zeb instructions, Yor wishes Olka a great life on the other side and receives a hug as a thanks. Despite Yor's protests because of her soiled hands, Olka has her hug Gram, saying that her hands are the reason he has a future. Yor appreciates the gesture and embraces the child, remarking how warm he is. Before leaving, Olka says she will pray for Yor and her family to find peace and happiness.[1]

ADVERTISEMENT

Relationships

Gram Gretcher

Olka motivated by Gram
Olka being strong for her son
Gram is Olka's only son, whom she named after her father. After the Gretcher Crime Family falls and her family members are killed due to infighting, Olka becomes tired of the gangster life and decides she simply wants to live a quiet life with Gram. After changing her appearance, Olka is amazed that Gram still recognizes her as his mother, but admits to being a little sad that she will never be told how much they like alike due to her different face. Olka wishes only the best for her son and tries to put up a brave front for him as their group encounters many threats throughout their stay on the cruise ship.

Zeb

Young Olka and Zeb
Olka and Zeb in their youth
In the past, Olka saved Zeb from starvation when she found him on the street and secretly brought him bread. Since then, Zeb has been deeply loyal to Olka, continuing to follow her despite being given the safer opportunity to follow the new boss who took over her family's organization. Olka is touched that Zeb chose to stay with her due to personal reasons, but is disappointed when he acts cowardly, even urging Gram not to grow up to be like him. When Zeb risks his life and takes three bullets to the back to protect Olka and her son, Olka is initially terrified for his life, but after he reveals he wore a bulletproof vest, she scolds him for being reckless. She is oblivious to his crush on her.

Yor Forger

Yor Forger is tasked with protecting Olka aboard the Princess Lorelei. When the two women first meet, Olka initially recognizes Yor simply as her bodyguard, calling her "one of them." However, as they talk more, Olka convinces Yor to let her and Gram outside for a bit and learns that Yor is also a mother, as her husband and child are also aboard the ship. Olka sees Yor visibly worried about being seen by her family and asks if they are just a cover for her. Seeing Yor's reaction and answer to her question, Olka appears to empathize with her feelings and gives her a disguise for them to wear outside their room, calling themselves "two mom friends hanging out." As they head back, Yor promises to complete her job without fail and protect Olka and Gram. Olka is touched and reciprocates by revealing Gram's name, even offering to let Yor hold him.

Olka thanks Yor
Olka thanks Yor
On the night of their first day, Yor and Olka discuss their plan to protect her, after which Yor says Gram can play as much as he wants after they are confirmed to be safe. Olka comments that Yor does not seem to be the underworld type and asks what she will do after their bodyguard mission is complete, then suggests that Yor could spend the last day of the cruise with her family on the resort island. In the end, Yor and Matthew successfully protect Olka and Gram from all the assassins. As they prepare to leave, Olka hugs Yor and expresses her gratefulness. She also has Yor hug Gram despite their protector's bloody hands, assuring her that those hands have guaranteed his future. Before parting ways, Olka tells Yor that she will pray for her and her family to find peace and happiness.

Isn't it strange? My face looks completely different, but he still recognizes me as his mother. Is it my voice? My smell? I supposed his vision isn't fully developed. I'm a little sad that no one will ever tell me how much we look alike… Besides, he looks more like his father than me.
OLKA GRETCHER TO YOR FORGER ABOUT GRAM[1]

Gram Gretcher (グラマ・グレッチャー, Guram Gurecchā?) is the only son of Olka Gretcher and one of the two remaining members of the Gretcher family. Yor Forger was tasked to protect Gram and Olka while aboard the Princess Lorelei.


ADVERTISEMENT
Appearance


00:00

41:20

Gram is a baby with short but well-groomed brown hair. He shares his mother's face, as they appear to have the same eyes, and after Olka had to change her appearance, they look more similar to each other. According to Olka, Gram resembles his late father.
Personality

While Gram is still a baby, he is very expressive. Like any other child, he is easily startled and is quick to cry. At times he shares his mother's feelings, such as when she was disappointed in how cowardly Zeb was acting or when the two thanked Yor for all of her help. Despite their situation, Gram found excitement when Yor jumped a big height while carrying him and his mother or saving them from an attacker.
History

Olka Gretcher Original Appearance Anime
Olka (before changing her appearance) and Gram
The Gretcher family used to manage Ostania's underworld in an honorable fashion. After the second war between Ostania and Westalis, the family ran a black market that distributed food to people on the streets. After years of serving, Olka married and had a son, who she named Gram, after her father. However, Gram's father and the rest of the Gretcher family were killed in an internal dispute, and the man who took over the family organization, Leonardo Hapoon, put a bounty on Gram and Olka's heads. The two went into hiding with the help of Zeb, a subordinate of the old boss, and stayed at a safe house. As a favor to their family, the Shopkeeper assigned Yor to protect them aboard Princess Lorelei while they escape to a foreign country by sea.
ADVERTISEMENT

Synopsis

Cruise Adventure Arc

Episode 30-6
Olka (after changing her appearance) and Gram
Aboard Princess Lorelei, Zeb presents himself as Furseal Grey, Gram as his kid and Olka as his wife to Yor Forger and Matthew McMahon. Yor accompanies them to their room as Olka cites the need to take care of her baby, and as the group splits up, Furseal expresses concern for leaving Olka and Gram alone, but Matthew assures him that Yor is strong.

Now alone with Olka and Gram, Yor inspects the suite for possible entry and escape routes. Yor talks with Olka, who says Furseal is a member of her crew playing a part, and explains how her family was killed, except her son Gram, and says she only desires a quiet life now. Gram, noticing his mother getting sad, starts to cry. As Olka calms him, they decide to go outside to grab some fresh air, but Yor explains her family is on the cruise too. As Olka and Yor talk about her family, Gram cries again, reminding them of their plan to go outside.

Yor meets Gram Gretcher
Olka presents Gram to Yor
When they go outside for fresh air, Olka and Gram enjoy the breeze and the view, wistful about leaving their old life behind. Gram starts to sneeze, so they decide to head back. Yor promises to give it her all and finish the job for Olka and her son. Her words move Olka, so she reveals her son's name and offers to let Yor hold him, but when Yor does so, Gram starts to cry, and Yor gives him back.[1]

Later, the City Hall group and the Grey family have dinner at a fancy restaurant. After dinner, Yor escorts Olka and Gram back to their room. Once inside, Olka notes there has not been any sign of trouble the entire day, but Yor warns her that they must keep their guard up as they have no idea of where the enemy is or their plan. While the two women talk, Gram is resting in his mother's arms. As Olka decides to change for the night, she puts Gram softly in bed, but suddenly they hear someone knocking on the door.[2]

Yor saves the Gretchers from gun shots
Yor moves Olka and Gram out of the line of fire
Yor looks through the peephole and sees a waiter with room service. Yor is relieved and tells Olka about this, but she says she did not order anything. Yor hears a gun click behind the door and quickly moves Olka to safety, so she quickly moves to the bed and holds a crying Gram. After the assassin is killed and his corpse is retrieved, Matthew informs the group that the itinerary got leaked and there are multiple enemies aboard the ship. He directs Yor to take Olka, Gram, and Zeb to a vacant room. After receiving domino masks to disguise themselves, Yor, Olka, Gram, and Zeb, leave for the second deck lounge.

Yor, Zeb, and the Gretchers cross paths with Barnaby
Gram and the others cross paths with Barnaby
The group head to a masquerade ball to blend in with the crowd. Upon arriving, an assassin is dispatched to kill Olka, but Yor stops him, grabbing his hand. She acts as if she was invited to a dance and dances the man away from Olka. Yor crushes the assassin's hand and knocks him unconscious to a seat. Yor returns to Olka, Furseal, and a scared Gram, and they decide to go through the shopping promenade to the second-class area, where they encounter Sickle-and-Chain Barnaby, who is defeated by Yor.[3]

As soon as they arrive at their new room, Gram starts to cry after being so scared, so Olka tries to comfort him, despite being scared herself. Furseal notices this and exclaims how terrified he was of their attackers. Olka and Gram jokingly disapprove of Zeb’s cowardice, while he is satisfied seeing them calm down.

Olka asks Zeb why he came with them instead of joining the gang's new boss. Zeb says he does not forget how much he owes to the previous boss and promises to protect them from harm. He relapses when he hears a knock on the door, and he quickly hides behind Olka while she and Gram look at him with indifferent expressions. The group rests for the night, with only Zeb and Gram asleep.[4]

Episode 32-6
Gram travels with his mother, Zeb and Yor on the ship
On the next day, the group waits until the night and receives a call from Matthew, telling them that he got the all-ready signal from the ship at the rendezvous. While the rendezvous will be in four hours, Yor, Olka, Gram, and Zeb change into disguises and head out of their room.[5]

Their plan is to head to the emergency exit at the ship's fore, where they can leave for the rendezvous. As they walk through the ship, Yor says they have to be as quiet as possible, so Olka gently hushes Gram. The fireworks show begins the moment they head up to the deck, and the group gets startled by the sudden noise, especially Gram, who starts crying. Olka coos to her baby, telling him how beautiful the fireworks look, while Gram hugs her in fear. After calming down, they continue onward. They reach a ladder, so Yor grabs Olka and Gram and jumps all the way up, surprising and entertaining Gram. From above, a sniper watches them and prepares to shoot Olka as another firework goes off. Yor quickly grabs Olka and Gram out of the way and fights off another assassin's attack. Suddenly, a large number of assassins reveal themselves and surround the group, and Olka holds onto her son tightly.[6]

Zeb protects Olka and Gram
Zeb uses his body to shield Gram and Olka
As the assassins surround the group, Yor tells Olka to hide with Gram and Zeb inside a hatch. While Olka and Gram go inside the hatch, an assassin points his gun at them. Zeb sees this and grabs Olka, shielding her from the bullets fired. As they tumble inside the hatch, Zeb shuts the cover. Gram starts crying in fright, and a worried Olka asks Zeb if he is okay, and he complains about how badly he is hurting even while wearing a bulletproof vest, so Olka tells him not to be so reckless. As soon as Gram sees Zeb is alright, he stops crying.[7]

Yor and Gram's goodbye hug
Yor says goodbye to Gram
After Yor and Matthew finish off all the assassins, Yor gets Gram, Olka, and Zeb from the hatch, and the group head to the emergency exit room. There, Yor and Matthew prepare the inflatable boat for them. Before leaving, Olka and Gram show their gratitude to Yor as Olka draws Gram into Yor's arms so she can hug him, saying that her hands are the reason her baby has a future. Yor appreciates the gesture and embraces Gram, remarking how warm he is.[8]

ADVERTISEMENT

Relationships

Olka Gretcher

As Olka is his mother, Gram deeply loves her and even recognizes her as such after she changed her appearance. It is said that babies get to connect with their mother's feelings, and Gram usually reflected any emotion Olka felt during their time on the cruise.

Yor Forger

Yor was given the task of protecting Olka and Gram while aboard Princess Lorelei. While on the cruise, Yor got to interact a little bit with Gram and even held him, remarking how warm he was. Even a couple of times, Gram cheered for Yor when she grabbed Olka and him and protected them

Back after the war, when there wasn't any food… I'd been dead in the streets if it wasn't for the black market your family ran. To this day, I can still taste that bread. That's all the reason I need to be here with you.
ZEB TO OLKA GRETCHER[1]

Zeb (ゼブ, Zebu?) is the friend of Olka Gretcher and a loyal follower of the Gretcher family. He pretended to be the husband of Olka (who was using the name Shaty Grey) under the alias Furseal Grey ( ファーシル・グレイ, Fāshiru Gurei?) while aboard the Princess Lorelei cruise ship.


ADVERTISEMENT
Appearance


00:01

41:20

Zeb is a tall man with slicked-back blond hair and purple eyes. Throughout his appearances, he continues to change clothes due to his and Olka's efforts to evade her assassins:

When meeting Yor Forger and the Berlint City Hall team, he wears a well-tailored suit jacket with a striped shirt. Later at a formal dinner, he wears a blue suit with a black shirt and white tie. When preparing to move out to reach the rendezvous, Zeb dons a light brown suit with a dark blue bow tie and a flower-shaped pin on his lapel, and also combs his hair down with a fringe covering his forehead.

When Zeb was younger, he had maroon hair.
Personality

Zeb is a kind but cowardly man who does his best to protect the people he cares about. Despite his fears, Zeb is willing to put himself on the line for Olka and Gram, as shown when he shields them from a gunman. He is also seen to be quite good at acting while not under pressure, as he played Olka's husband during their time on Princess Lorelei.

He is seen as rather nervous and anxious when under pressure, to the point he could not taste the food during dinner or drink alcohol due to the threat of being targeted by several assassins. Zeb is also very cautious in his mission to protect Olka. He initially doubted Yor's ability as a bodyguard after believing she was not fit for her line of work and felt uncomfortable leaving only her with Olka in her room.
ADVERTISEMENT

History

Young Olka and Zeb
Zeb and Olka's first meeting
Not much is told about Zeb's past, but from his memories, it can be seen that as a child, he and his family were in poverty due to the losses that the second war between Ostania and Westalis caused them, and Zeb recalls how he would have been dead if not for the black market the Gretcher family ran after the war, remembering fondly the memory of a young Olka secretly giving him bread. From there, Zeb developed feelings for Olka and joined the Gretcher crime family.

After the Gretcher family fell due to infighting, Leonardo Hapoon took over. Disliking Hapoon for cozying up to pro-war extremists to get rich, Zeb chose to not work for him and stayed loyal to Olka. After Hapoon places a bounty on Olka and Gram's heads, Olka gets help from the assassin organization Garden to board Princess Lorelei in order to seek asylum in a foreign country, and Zeb decides to join her. Three days before they board the ship, Zeb makes a phone call to his parents to say goodbye.
ADVERTISEMENT
Synopsis

Cruise Adventure Arc

Matthew and Yor meet Zeb and the Gretchers
Zeb and the Gretchers meet Matthew and Yor
In the first-class suite, Matthew McMahon introduces himself as the Director of Policy at Berlint City Hall and two bureaucrats from their business development team, Heymann and Vides, including Yor. Zeb introduces himself "Furseal Grey" from Arhaus Department Stores and Olka as his wife, "Shaty." Furseal observes that Yor must be Olka's assigned bodyguard and worries if she can protect Olka after seeing her slim appearance, but Matthew assures him that Yor is strong.[2]

The city hall group and the Grey family have dinner at a fancy restaurant. While the group chats about how good the food is, Yor and Furseal fidget around, too nervous to taste anything. After dinner, the men head down to the lower deck for drinks while Yor escorts Olka and Gram back to their room.

Matthew and Zeb rush to the Gretchers and Yor
Matthew pulls Zeb aside to inform him of the danger at hand
Nearby, Zeb, Matthew, and the other men walk around after drinking at the bar. Matthew suddenly excuses himself for a moment and quickly takes Zeb away upon returning, informing him that Olka's information has circulated among their assassin pursuers. Because of the secrecy of the operation, there is no way the information could have leaked, so Matthew asks Zeb if he made any contact with the outside world while hiding. Zeb mentions the phone call he made to his parents but swears that he did not tell them anything important.[3]

Matthew and Zeb arrive at the room, where an assassin has already made his attack. After Matthew catches the assassin's attention, the assassin aims at him Matthew and Zeb, but Yor hurls her weapon through the door and pins his head to the wall, killing him. After retrieving the corpse, Matthew informs the group that the itinerary got leaked and there are multiple enemies aboard the ship. He directs Yor to take Zeb, Olka, and Gram to a vacant room in the second-class suite while he covers up the mess. He forewarns her that the ship might return to port if there is a public incident and recommends she avoid fighting to prevent that. After receiving domino masks to disguise themselves, Yor, Olka, Zeb, and Gram leave for the second deck lounge.

Yor, Zeb, and the Gretchers cross paths with Barnaby
The group crosses paths with Sickle-and-Chain Barnaby
While walking through the halls, Zeb says the masks make them look conspicuous, and Yor assures him that the second lounge is holding a masquerade ball, where they will blend in. She also notices that they are being followed and discloses this with the others. Upon arriving at the ball, Yor dispatches attacking assassins without causing any disturbance, and upon finishing, she returns to the group, and they go through the shopping promenade to the second-class area.[4] Olka, Gram, Zeb, and Yor cross paths with Sickle-and-Chain Barnaby, who swings his blade at them in a surprise attack. Yor moves, ducking the attack while moving Zeb and Olka with her, and the two begin to fight.[5] Zeb flees the scene with the Gretchers, and when Yor defeats Barnaby, she returns to the three after ditching Barnaby at a seat.[6]

Young Zeb Anime
Zeb's younger self in his memory
After arriving at their new room, Yor assures the group that it is secure and has everything they need to hole up safely until the rendezvous. Zeb notices Olka and Gram are visibly shaken, so he exclaims how scared he was to calm them down, and his attempt succeeds, although at his expense. Olka asks Zeb why he came with them instead of joining the gang's new boss. Zeb explains that it is because he owes a lot to the previous boss and recalls what Olka and her family have done for him. Zeb remembers it fondly and says it is all the reason he needs to be with her. Zeb promises to protect Olka from harm but relapses when he hears a knock on the door and quickly hides behind Olka. Behind the door is Matthew, who tells the two to rest while he whittles down the enemy numbers. Zeb is baffled by how composed the assassins are and says that despite the war officially ending over a decade ago, war is still around. Matthew replies that as long as people are the way they are, the fighting will never stop and that he and Yor are soldiers fighting for their country.[1]

Episode 32-6
The group move out to prepare for the rendezvous
Standing by a radio, Matthew receives a transmission and calls Olka's room. Yor answers the phone and informs the others that they got the all-ready signal from the ship at the rendezvous. While it will be in four hours, Yor tells Olka and Zeb to prepare and change into their disguises. After seeing that the coast is clear, Yor, Olka, Gram, and Zeb head out.[7]

As the fireworks show is about to commence, the group walks through the halls of the ship. Yor says their destination is Storage Area 3 and explains the plan to get Olka and Zeb off the boat and to the rendezvous ship, hoping to proceed during the fireworks show, but the show starts, and the group is startled by the sudden noise. After calming down, they continue onward. From above, a sniper watches them and prepares to shoot Olka as another firework goes off. Yor quickly grabs Olka out of the way but gets grazed by the shot. Yor asks Olka and Zeb if they are alright. Suddenly, a large number of assassins reveal themselves and surround the group.[8]

Zeb protects Olka and Gram
Zeb uses his body to shield Olka and Gram
As the assassins surround Zeb, Olka, Yor, and Gram, Yor tells them to hide inside a hatch, but she gets held back by a rope user when she tries to guide them there. While Olka and Gram go inside the hatch, an assassin points his gun at them. Zeb sees this and grabs Olka, shielding her from the bullets fired. As they tumble inside the hatch, Zeb shuts the cover. A worried Olka asks Zeb if he is okay, and he complains about how badly he is hurting even while wearing a bulletproof vest, and Olka tells him not to be so reckless.[9]

After Yor and Matthew deal with all the assassins, Olka, Gram and Zeb are taken out of the hatch and go to the storage area. Yor and Matthew prepare the inflatable boat for them to reach the rendezvous and Matthew gives Zeb instructions to stay safe. After bidding goodbye to their bodyguards, Zeb, Olka, and Gram leave Princess Lorelei.[10]

ADVERTISEMENT

Relationships

Olka Gretcher

Zeb tells Olka why he does not want to work with Hapoon
A blushing Zeb talks with Olka
Zeb is a loyal follower to Olka, continuing to follow her despite being given the safer opportunity to follow Leonardo Hapoon after he took over her family's organization. They first met when they were kids during the aftermath of the East-West war, where she gave him a piece of bread. Zeb has a crush on Olka, though she appears to be oblivious to his feelings. However, even in those moments when Zeb almost gives himself away, he blushes and tries in every possible way to hide his feelings under other reasons why he should be with her.

Zeb deeply cares for Olka, as when he noticed that she was still scared after the first attack from the enemy assassins, Zeb exaggerates his fear to help her and Gram calm down, and later uses his own body to shield her and Gram when they are getting shot at.

Yor Forger

Zeb was initially doubtful of Yor's abilities to protect Olka, but after watching her strength, he trusts her as a capable bodyguard to protect and help them survive until their rendezvous.

entries.name: Cavi Campbell
entries.content: Cavi Campbell is a 56-year-old man who is the father of Carrol and Kim Campbell. He is known as one of the world's foremost collectors of classical art after obtaining a fortune in the energy sector. He is also one of the organizers of Campbelldon, an underground tennis competition. He is the main antagonist of the Campbelldon Tennis Arc.

Carrol Campbell (キャロル・キャンベル, Kyaroru Kyanberu?) is the son of Cavi Campbell and the older twin brother of Kim Campbell. He is one of the antagonists of the Campbelldon Tennis Arc, being Twilight and Nightfall's final opponents in the Campbelldon.

Appearance

Carrol is a young man of average height. He has blond hair, which he slicks back with a strand of hair hanging on the right side of his face.

His tennis attire consists of a blue-gray low V-neck shirt with a collar, white tennis shorts, and red wristbands. Strapped at the back of his waist, he wears a small black pack with a cord connected to his modified tennis racket, which likely powers it.
Personality

Carrol is a cocky and arrogant person, confident in his tennis skills. He has a strong desire to win, to the point of using underhanded tricks to get the upper hand on his opponents and ensure his victory. However, after he and his sister lose to Loid and Fiona during the Campbelldon, he is humbled by the experience and swears to train hard to become a great tennis player using his own strength.
History

Carrol is a high school student. According to Loid's information, Carrol and his sister Kim have been playing tennis since early childhood and participated in their father's underground tennis tournament, the Campbelldon, where they achieved two consecutive victories.
Synopsis

Campbelldon Tennis Arc

Carrol hits the ball back
Carrol using his jet-powered tennis racket
Kim and Carrol, playing as a team, defeated every opponent they played against, easily reaching the finals against Loid and Fiona, who are undercover as the Foney couple. As the start of the final match begins, the odds are in the Foneys' favor, but Cavi bets ten million on his children. Carrol tells Kim that he got word from their father that they do not need to make the game look close this time which Kim is pleased about, as she is eager to get the match over with and get the new yacht that Cavi promised them. Carrol pulls out his jet-powered tennis racket and Kim her whip racket. When Loid serves the ball, Carrol returns it to Fiona with lots of force from the rockets, and Fiona ends up landing it out of bounds. Carrol tells them not to think of it as cheating as he had to practice a lot to learn how to use it.

In the next game, Loid makes a serve that neither of the siblings will seemingly be able to reach. However, Kim releases a latch on her racket, allowing it to extend far enough to hit the ball, and drives it down onto the other side of the court, scoring them a point. Using these special rackets, the siblings continue to win the first two games and, thus, the first set of the match. As the second set begins, Carrol serves with a powerful hit, followed by a return from Loid. Kim tries to hit the ball with some spin, but Fiona quickly returns it, scoring a point. As they continue playing, Loid and Fiona win three more sets.

Fiona hits a tennis ball to Carrol's side
Carrol misses Fiona's serve
Knowing they will lose at this rate, Carrol looks over to a suited man on the sidelines, who gives him a nod before fiddling with a control panel. In the next game, a floor tile under Fiona's foot sinks into the ground as she makes her serve, causing her to hit it out of bounds.[2] More sunken floor tiles are used against Loid, who avoids them and manages to score a point. Carrol then tries hitting the ball in another sunken tile and bouncing it back in his direction. To his shock, however, Fiona intercepts it and slams it to the ground, scoring another point.

Carrol decides to change plans: manipulating the net's height. He signals to the staff, and they comply. Loid and Fiona notice the changes and opt to work around them. When the Campbells realize their tricks are not working, they try using more against the Foneys, from gusts of wind to coating the ball with stink spray. However, all their schemes only amounted to little more than a slight annoyance to the Foneys, who win the set and tie the scores.

Carrol's Signal
Carrol signaling to the sniper to shoot
With the deciding set upon them, the frustrated Campbell siblings decide to "call in the big guns." The game begins, and as Fiona is about to make her return, Carrol quickly sticks out his tongue and moves it around, signaling to a sniper hiding in the vents to shoot Fiona. To everyone's surprise, Loid tackles Fiona to the ground, taking the bullet for her. Carrol jokes about them being touchy but is amazed that Loid saw the bullet coming. He is even more amazed when he sees Loid get up and walk off from being shot. When Carrol hears that Loid is apparently suffering from a hangover, he is astounded and finds it unbelievable.

The game resumes, and Carrol makes another signal to attack Loid mid-serve. Loid staggers to the side and finishes his serve, surprising everyone. The sniper radios to the "court interference squad" for assistance, telling them to do whatever it takes to ensure the siblings win. Their tricks do not work on the agents, who predict their moves and move around them. The sniper even calls in the ball boys to make their move, but the extra interference fails to stop the Foneys. Seeing all this, a frustrated Cavi yells at his children to get it together and beat their opponents, as he has a lot riding on this match.

Carrol's Loss
Carrol loses to Loid
The ball and a bullet are shot at Loid, who returns them with a swing. The parried bullet hits Carrol in the stomach and staggers him, and he claims to the line judge that he had too much milk in the morning, resulting in stomach cramps. Seeing that both teams appear impaired in the final stretch, the commentator calls the match a battle of sheer will as the audience cheers. While they play, Carrol thinks about how he does not want to lose and be beaten by Loid but sees that he is no match for him. Loid jumps up in front of Carrol, intimidating him with his aura as he slams the ball under the boy's frozen legs.

With that, the Foneys win the championship match, and the men betting on them stand up and cheer while Cavi sinks into his seat. Carrol approaches Loid, realizing that despite being aware of the tricks, the Foneys still won. Carrol tears up and confesses that this is the first time he is disappointed in himself. Loid encourages Carrol, who is young and talented, and by working hard to hone his skills, he can become a great player one day. Carrol swears to train hard, and Loid cheers him on.[3]

Abilities and Skills

Carrol uses his jet-powered tennis racket
Carrol uses his jet-powered tennis racket
Tennis Skills: Like his sister, Carrol has practiced tennis from a very young age, developing good reflexes and speed, being able to defeat all the competitors in the tennis tournament alongside his brother. Even up until the final match against the Foneys, the twins mention that during every match they were holding back.

Physical Strength: As mentioned, Carrol has great agility and skill in tennis, but highlights that he was able to control a jet-powered tennis racket in his final game against the Foneys, keeping up a good match while also controlling the force of both hitting and returning the blows to Loid and Fiona.
Relationships

Kim Campbell

Carrol has been training in tennis with his younger twin sister since they were young. Not much can be seen about their relationship with each other, but they viewed the sport they played differently, as Carrol was very passionate about it and sought to win at any cost, whereas Kim found it lame and only played for their father's awards for winning.

Loid Forger

Campbelldon Finale
Carrol is motivated by Loid to become a great tennis player
Knowing him as "Twain Foney," Carrol initially saw Loid as someone below his skill level. However, as their match progressed, Carrol saw the gap between them, even while using underhanded tricks to get the upper hand. After losing, he admitted to Loid that it was the first time in his life that he felt disappointed in himself. To his surprise, Loid motivates him to work hard to become a great tennis player, moving Carrol as he swears to Loid thard.

KIM TO CARROL CAMPBELL[1]

Kim Campbell (キム・キャンベル, Kimu Kyanberu?) is the daughter of Cavi Campbell and the younger twin sister of Carrol Campbell. She is one of the antagonists of the Campbelldon Tennis Arc, being Twilight and Nightfall's final opponents in the Campbelldon.


ADVERTISEMENT
Appearance

Kim is a young woman of average height. She has long blonde hair, which she ties into a ponytail while a strand of hair hangs on the right side of her face. Over her forehead, she wears a white headband.

Her tennis attire consists of a light pink tennis dress with a belt at her waist and white wristbands. She also wears drop earrings with a tennis ball design and a gold necklace with a similar design at the center. Strapped at the back of her waist, she wears a small black pack with a cord connected to her modified tennis racket, which likely powers it.
Personality

Despite playing the sport since early childhood, Kim appears to not be very engaged in it. When they lost the finals match between the Foneys, she found her brother's passion lame and decided she was done with tennis. However, she did desire to win, but mainly for the reward their father promised them if they won the match.
History

Kim is a high school student. According to Loid's information, Kim and her brother Carrol have been playing tennis since early childhood and participated in their father's underground tennis tournament, the Campbelldon, where they achieved two consecutive victories.
ADVERTISEMENT

Synopsis

Campbelldon Tennis Arc

Kim and Carrol, playing as a team, defeated every opponent they played against (sometimes with the help of their father's interference), easily reaching the finals against Loid and Fiona, who are undercover as the Foney couple. As the start of the final match begins, the odds are in the Foneys' favor, but Cavi bets ten million on his children. Carrol tells Kim that he got word from their father that they do not need to make the game look close this time which Kim is pleased about. She is eager to get the match over and get the new yacht that Cavi promised them. Carrol pulls out his jet-powered tennis racket, and Kim pulls out her whip racket. When Loid serves the ball, Carrol returns it to Fiona with lots of force from the rockets, and Fiona ends up landing it out of bounds.

Kim's Whip Racket
Kim reaches Loid's serve using her whip racket

However, Kim releases a latch on her racket, allowing it to extend far enough to hit the ball, and drives it down onto the other side of the court, scoring them a point. Using these special rackets, the siblings continue to win the first two games and thus the first set of the match. As the second set begins, Carrol serves with a powerful hit, followed by a return from Loid. Kim tries to hit the ball with some spin, but Fiona quickly returns it, scoring a point. As they continue playing, Loid and Fiona win three more sets.[2]

The Foneys maintain the advantage and score another point. Carrol decides to change plans: manipulating the net's height. He signals to the staff, and they comply. Loid and Fiona notice the changes and opt to work around them. When the Campbells realize their tricks are not working, they try using more against the Foneys, from gusts of wind to coating the ball with stink spray, to Kim's frustration. All their schemes only amount to little more than a slight annoyance to the Foneys, who win the set and tie the scores.

Episode 23-5
Loid serves the ball to the twins with a staggering serve
The frustrated Campbell siblings decide to "call in the big guns." As the game begins, Loid notices a sniper hidden in the vents aiming at Fiona. Loid moves quickly, tackling Fiona as he takes the bullet and tumbles to the ground, surprising everyone, especially the Campbell twins, who wonder if the couple found out about their plan. The game resumes, and Loid, who has seen through their latest scheme, begins to stagger to the side as he makes his serve, surprising everyone. The sniper radios to the "court interference squad" for assistance, telling them to do whatever it takes to ensure the Campbell siblings win. Their tricks do not work on the agents, who predict their moves and move around them, even after extra interference from the court is added.

Kim's disinterest in losing

The parried bullet hits Carrol in the stomach and staggers him, and he claims to the judge that he now has stomach cramps. Seeing that both teams appear impaired in the final stretch, the commentator calls the match a battle of sheer will as the audience cheers. In the last point, Loid slams the ball under Carrol's legs. With that, the Foneys win the championship match. After the game, Carrol approaches Loid and expresses his frustration at himself for losing. Loid encourages Carrol to work hard to hone his skills so he can become a great player one day. While Carrol is moved, Kim finds the whole thing lame and decides that she is done with tennis.[3]

ADVERTISEMENT

Abilities and Skills

Tennis Skills: Like her brother, Kim has practiced tennis from a very young age, developing good reflexes and speed, being able to control a whip racket and defeat all the competitors in the tennis tournament alongside her brother. Even up until the final match against the Foneys, the twins mention that during every match they were holding back.
Relationships

Carrol Campbell

Kim has been training in tennis with her older brother since they were young. However, she was not as passionate about the sport compared to him and decided to quit after their loss to the Foneys.

MURDOCH SWAN TO YOR FORGER[1]

Murdoch Swan (マードック・スワン, Mūdokku Suwan?) is the Economics Teacher and Housemaster of Dormitory 2, Cline Hall at Eden Academy. He is the only son of the school's former headmaster and is regarded as arrogant, greedy, and callous. One month before the Eden Academy admissions interview, his wife filed for divorce and won full custody of their only daughter, leaving him resentful of happy families.


ADVERTISEMENT
Appearance

Murdoch is a stout, middle-aged man. He has black hair that is receding, small eyebrows, and a thick walrus mustache. He wears a navy blue suit (dark brown in the anime) with a striped tie.
Personality

Murdoch is regarded as an arrogant, greedy, and callous man. As the son of Eden's former headmaster, Murdoch is well aware of the influence his father still has in the school and unabashedly flaunts it, using it to threaten Henry Henderson when he opposes his methods and even going as far to claim Eden as his. Due to his own unhappy history with his family, Murdoch is resentful of happy families. As such, during the admissions interview, he tries to find and exploit weaknesses in families he dislikes to prevent them from entering the school because to him, allowing them in would mean there is no "justice" in the world.

Murdoch provokes Yor
Murdoch gleefully provokes Yor after making Anya cry
When interviewing the Forger family, Murdoch is immediately jealous of their perfect appearance and does everything he can to tear them down and stop them from entering Eden. He questions Yor's decision to marry a man with a child and later humiliates her as he insults her ability as a wife upon learning that she does not cook. After making Anya cry by rudely asking which of her two mothers she preferred, Murdoch took glee in her sadness and Yor's anger, which he found refreshing. He momentarily drops his facade after Loid almost strikes him, but quickly collects himself while angrily yelling at the Forgers as they leave the interview. After getting punched by Henry for his actions, Murdoch is disappointed when he is only demoted to teaching the new first-years, likely wanting to have him fired instead.

Murdoch's uncouth behavior seems to influence some of his students, as two boys from Cline Hall were punished by Donna Schlag for bad behavior and other infractions.
ADVERTISEMENT

History

Murdoch Swan was born to the previous headmaster of Eden Academy, and he is the man's only son. With his father's influence, he secured a job at the prestigious school and taught Economics. Eventually, he also became the housemaster of Cline Hall. At some point in his life, Murdoch got married and had a daughter. However, this family did not appear to be the best, as one month before Eden's admissions interview, his wife filed for divorce and won full custody of their daughter. This event caused Murdoch to become resentful of happy families and take his frustrations out on them because of his jealousy.
Synopsis

Admissions Interview Arc

The Forgers at the family interview
Murdoch, Walter, and Henry interview the Forgers
On the day of the family interviews for the Eden Academy admissions, Murdoch serves an interviewer alongside fellow teachers and housemasters Walter Evans and Henry Henderson. In one of the interviews, Murdoch intimidates a young applicant for being unable to answer some questions, after which Walter ends up dismissing the applicant and his family from the room. The next family called in is the Forgers, who give off a good impression to Walter and Henry. Murdoch, however, makes crude comments, asking why Yor married Loid while knowing he had a child. Later, when Loid comments that he does most of the cooking at their home, Murdoch is shocked that Yor does not cook and begins belittling her, prompting Loid to defend her. Jealous of the couple's relationship, Murdoch swears to himself to keep picking at them until they slip up, believing there is no justice in the world if they pass.

Loid losing control after Murdoch's words
Loid almost strikes Murdoch for smearing his family
After Anya gives her parents good ratings, Murdoch scoffs at everyone's feelings and cruelly asks her who she likes better: Yor or her first mother. When Walter protests, Murdoch justifies his position to improvise his questions. Anya then begins crying for her mother, which Murdoch takes glee in before reasoning that Eden cannot have children who cry over every little thing. This angers Yor, whom Murdoch continues to taunt, saying that it is not his fault Anya loves her less. His words finally get to Loid and make him almost punch Murdoch, but he smashes the table between them instead, which terrifies Murdoch.

Henry punches Murdoch Swan
Murdoch is knocked out cold by Henry for his arrogance
After claiming he punched a mosquito on the table, Loid admonishes Murdoch and the other teachers for belittling the feelings of children, then promptly leaves with his family. An enraged Murdoch yells at Loid for disgracing Eden's name and declares that they will never set foot in "his" school again. Murdoch is confronted by Henry, who tells him he has gone too far. In response, Murdoch threatens to have Henry punished for questioning his methods using his father's influence. As Murdoch demands to bring in the next family, Henry suddenly steps forward and tells Murdoch that he was the one who disgraced Eden before punching him square in the face and knocking him out cold.[1]

On the day of Eden's acceptance list posting, Henry meets with the Forgers to inform them that Anya is at the top of the school's waiting list thanks to his discretion, citing that Loid saved Murdoch's life from the mosquito he killed. Henry also adds that he may lose his teaching position at Eden due to punching Murdoch and wonders how the man's father will punish him.[2]

Eden Beginnings Arc

Eden Academy Orientation Day Anime
Murdoch attending the school orientation
While Yor spends time with Anya after getting the latter's school uniform, she sees other mothers planning to make dinner for their children, which makes her recall the interview and Murdoch's comments that Anya loves her real mother better. His words lowers Yor's mood, but they also inspire her to try being a better mother for Anya.[3]

On the day of Eden's orientation ceremony, Murdoch sits with the other teachers. Much to his disappointment, Henry is still teaching at Eden, though he has been demoted to teaching a class of first year students. As Henry is called forward to lead his new class, Murdoch scoffs in annoyance.[4]

WISE Arc

When Donna Schlag returns to Eden Academy, she wastes little time in resuming her punishing of the student body with Tonitrus Bolts. Two of her victims are boys from Murdoch's Cline Hall, whom she punishes for their unkempt uniforms, uncouth speech, and conspiring to commit acts of violence. After punishing them, Donna comments that Murdoch's students are all disgraces.[5]

Red Circus Arc

When Henry is shocked by Anya's casualness in the hijacked bus, Murdoch briefly appears in his memory while recalling Anya's resolve to reach the headmaster's position during the admissions interview.[6]

ADVERTISEMENT

Relationships

Henry Henderson

Murdoch threatens Henry
Murdoch rudely advises Henry to watch his mouth
Murdoch and Henry are co-workers who do not have a good relationship. During the interview with the Forgers in the admissions exams, Henry disliked Murdoch's impolite questions and comments, although Murdoch himself chose to ignore his remark. After the interview escalated into Loid smashing the table after Murdoch further insulted his family, the Forgers left the interview, and Henry called Murdoch out for going too far. In response, Murdoch became angry that Henry would dare to criticize his methods and responded by threatening him with his father's influence. Murdoch rudely advised Henry to watch his mouth, but Henry refused to stand by and punched Murdoch in the face for disgracing Eden Academy, knocking the man out cold.

After this incident, Henry is not fired from Eden but instead put in charge of the first-year students of the new term, much to Murdoch's annoyance.
